proof_0001.moves: Says that isLeft of a left injection is true. isLeft is defined by matching on the constructor, so on inl it reduces to true outright; the whole proof is that definitional computation, closed by rfl. No mathematical idea beyond unfolding a definition on a constructor.

proof_0002.moves: Prop has at least two distinct elements. The proof exhibits witnesses: take True and False and cite that they are unequal. The content is entirely the choice of witnesses plus the fact true_ne_false.

proof_0003.moves: In a preorder, a < b implies a <= b. The proof invokes the preorder axiom that a < b is equivalent to a <= b and not b <= a, then projects the left half of the conjunction. Two steps: unfold < by the characterizing iff, take And.left.

proof_0004.moves: The app field of an applicative transformation coincides with its coercion to a function, because the CoeFun instance is defined to be exactly that field. Purely definitional, closed by rfl.

proof_0005.moves: A derivation kills 1. This is just the structure field map_one_eq_zero' restated in applied/coerced form; the proof is a direct citation of the primed version with no additional argument.

proof_0006.moves: De Morgan for a decidable conjunction. Forward direction case-splits on whether a holds: if it does, b must fail (feed the pair to the hypothesis) so take the right disjunct; if not, take the left disjunct. Backward direction is the constructive lemma not_and_of_not_or_not. The case split on decidability is the whole point of this version.

proof_0007.moves: A Hoare triple is a one-field structure wrapping the entailment P <= wp x Q, so the iff is pure unwrapping: constructor one way, destructuring match the other. No mathematical content, just the structure isomorphism.

proof_0008.moves: The sup on a Pi type is defined pointwise, so the stated equation is the defining equation of that instance; rfl. The content is naming which instance is being unfolded.

proof_0009.moves: 0 belongs to the pointwise zero set, which is the singleton {0}; membership there unfolds to 0 = 0, so reflexivity closes it. The real move is unfolding the definition of (0 : Set a) as a singleton, which nothing in the candidate list names.

proof_0010.moves: The opposite of the identity map on open neighbourhoods acts as the identity on objects. Both sides are already definitionally equal; the proof is `by simp`, whose trace is nothing but a reflexivity closure wrapped in of_eq_true. There is no mathematical step here.

proof_0011.moves: Lifting a computation along the reflexive MonadLiftT instance is the identity, so its weakest precondition is unchanged. Everything is definitional; rfl. The content is entirely that the refl lift instance computes to the identity.

proof_0012.moves: The first coordinate of an element embedded via inr is 0, because inr a is defined as the pair (0, a). Reading off a component of a definition; rfl.

proof_0013.moves: The top object-property contains a zero object: exhibit the zero object supplied by HasZeroObject as the witness, note it is a zero object (isZero_zero), and note that the top property holds of it trivially. Exhibiting the witness and discharging the trivial predicate is the whole proof.

proof_0014.moves: Comparing two left injections in the lexicographic sum order reduces to comparing the underlying elements. The order on the lex sum is definitionally Sum.Lex, so the statement is a direct restatement of the corresponding Lex lemma.

proof_0015.moves: The continuous map induced by the identity order homomorphism on the upper-set topology is the identity continuous map. The induced map is defined by conjugating with the identity type-synonym equivalences, so both bundled maps are literally the same term; rfl. Note the right-hand side ContinuousMap.id is not in the candidate list.

proof_0016.moves: The carrier of the complement SubMulAction is the set complement of the carrier. The Compl instance was defined with exactly that carrier, so this is its defining equation; rfl. The long chain of algebraic superclass projections is pure typeclass bookkeeping.

proof_0017.moves: Two dependent pairs (n, f) of Fin-indexed tuples are equal iff the lengths agree and the tuples agree after casting along that equality. Forward: substitute along the pair equality, take the length equality to be rfl, and prove the function equality pointwise by funext, destructing each Fin index so that Fin.cast computes away. Backward: the existing lemma sigma_eq_of_eq_comp_cast. The forward direction is substitution plus a pointwise rfl, which no citation really names.

proof_0018.moves: Monotonicity transfers to the WithBot-lifted map. This declaration is an alias for one direction of the existing iff characterization, so the proof is literally Iff.mpr applied to monotone_map_iff. No new argument.

proof_0019.moves: Dropping trailing elements failing p from a list with x appended, where p x is false, leaves the list untouched. Rewrite by the concat formula for rdropWhile, which produces an if-then-else on p x, then use the hypothesis with if_neg to select the else branch. Two rewrites; everything else is rewriting residue.

proof_0020.moves: The bundled inclusion relation embedding, coerced back to a function, is Set.inclusion. Its toFun field was defined to be exactly that, so unfolding the FunLike coercion gives it definitionally; rfl. Set.inclusion, the right-hand side, is absent from the candidate list.

proof_0021.moves: The byte index of a raw position advanced by a string. The declaration is a rename/alias of an identically stated lemma, so the proof is a single citation with no mathematical step of its own.

proof_0022.moves: Auto-generated obligation for the addition on a submonoid's subtype: the sum of the underlying values of two elements of S lies in S. Apply the closure-under-addition axiom to the two membership proofs carried by the subtype elements.

proof_0023.moves: A set is an antichain with least element a exactly when it is the singleton {a}. Forward: use the characterization of being a singleton by a unique member; a is a member by IsLeast, and any other member b satisfies a <= b as a is a lower bound, so the antichain condition forces b = a. Backward: substitute s = {a} and cite that a singleton is an antichain and that a is least in {a}.

proof_0024.moves: Casting an if-then-else of integers equals the if-then-else of the casts, because any function commutes with a branch on the same decidable condition. A direct instance of apply_ite with the cast as the function.
